### Observed differences

- The clearest change concerns the block A19 – A25 – A20. In the earlier window each of these activities took part in about 48 in 100 traces (roughly half an occurrence per trace); in the later window each takes part in about 199 of 200 traces and occurs about once per trace. [OCC003, OCC004, OCC005]
- Before, these activities were typically skipped together: for pairs among them, neither activity was present in about 51–53 in 100 traces. In the later window they co-occur in about 199 of 200 traces, keeping the same fixed order as before: A19 leads to A25 in about 93–97 in 100 of its observed outgoing transitions in both windows, A25 leads to A20 in about 96–99 in 100, and A19 precedes A20 in about 97 in 100 traces (about 46 in 100 before, measured over traces where both occurred). [REL018, REL019, REL022, DIR004, DIR005]
- A41 now feeds this block almost exclusively. Before, its observed outgoing transitions split between A26 (about 45 in 100) and A19 (about 37 in 100); in the later window about 96 in 100 go to A19, and A41 precedes A19, A25 and A20 in 96–97 in 100 traces, at event distances of about 1, 2 and 3 respectively. [DIR006, REL021, REL024, REL026, LAG018, LAG019, LAG020]
- A26 now follows the block. Before, A26 occurred without A19 in about 52 in 100 traces and often directly after A41 (distance 1 in about 46 in 100 of pairs); in the later window A19, A20 and A25 each precede A26 in about 97–99 in 100 traces, A41 reaches A26 at distance 4 in about 93 in 100 of pairs, and A26's mean relative event position moved slightly later (0.41 to 0.44). [REL020, REL023, REL025, LAG021, POS002]
- A06 takes part in about 73 in 100 traces, up from about 24 in 100, and appears early and consistently in the trace (median relative event position about 0.21 versus 0.39; upper quartile 0.26 versus 0.91). It now precedes A19, A20 and A25 in about 65 in 100 traces, whereas before, A06 and A19 co-occurred in only about 13 in 100 traces. [OCC001, POS001, REL004, REL005, REL006]
- A06's routing is now concentrated: about 88 in 100 of its observed outgoing transitions go to A16 (before, they were spread over many activities, the largest share about 21 in 100 to A15). A15 now routes to A06 in about 40 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (about 1 in 100 before), while A15 to A16 fell from about 94 to 58 in 100; A06-to-A16 pairs within five steps are almost always adjacent (about 97 in 100 of 136 pairs at distance 1), and A15-to-A06 pairs are most often at distance 1 as well. [DIR001, DIR003, LAG002, LAG009]
- A08 became rare: about 8 in 100 traces versus about 20 in 100 before, and the share of A14's outgoing transitions leading to A08 fell from about 4 in 100 to under 1 in 100. [OCC002, DIR002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that a sequence of activities that was previously skipped in about half of the cases — A41, then A19, then A25, then A20, with A26 after it — is executed in virtually every case in the later window, while its internal order stayed the same. In the earlier window the block ran in about 48 in 100 traces and was absent as a whole in the other half; in the later window A41 precedes A19, A25 and A20 in about 96–97 in 100 traces, the three activities run in a fixed order in almost every trace, and A26, which previously often occurred without the block or directly after A41, now consistently comes after it. [OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, REL018, REL019, REL022, REL020, REL021, DIR006, LAG021]

Supporting signs: the participation counts rest on roughly 95–199 traces per window; the pairwise relations move directly from "neither present" to near-universal co-occurrence with an unchanged order; and A41's and A26's routing changes point the same way. In total 62 control-flow items qualified against about 0.84 expected for an unchanged process, so chance sampling cannot account for the pattern as a whole, and every item's difference exceeds those of about 199 of 200 random re-splits of the pooled data. [OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, REL018, REL019, REL022, DIR006, LAG021]

Limitations: many relation items describe the same underlying trace behaviour and are not independent confirmations, and the two windows are finite samples. The evidence also cannot rule out that the later window simply contains a different mix of cases — for example only cases of a kind that always executes this block — rather than a change in the process itself. [REL018, REL019, REL022]

Other differences: A06 appears to be inserted into the flow between A15 and A16 — it takes part in about 73 in 100 traces (up from about 24 in 100), sits early in the trace, A15 now leads to it in about 40 in 100 of its outgoing transitions while A15 to A16 dropped to about 58 in 100, and A06 typically immediately precedes A16. A08 nearly disappeared (about 8 in 100 traces, down from about 20 in 100). A few other routing shares shifted only slightly, for example A14 to A15 (about 85 to 97 in 100 of outgoing transitions). [OCC001, DIR001, DIR003, LAG002, LAG009, REL004, OCC002, DIR002]
